comments.author: @therainman7777
comments.text:
More than any other model to date, GPT-5 feels like a model for which the benchmark scores are extremely misleading—in a good way. For many models, the benchmark scores are really high, but then you’re badly disappointed when you use the model for real-world use cases. GPT-5, on the other hand, has benchmark scores that are impressive, but not mind-blowing—and then you use it for real-world use cases and you have your mind blown. This is such a nice change of pace, where the benchmark scores undersell things, and the model over-delivers massively.

I feel people are not yet understanding just how big of a leap GPT-5 really is. From their perspective, it didn’t score 98% on SWE-Bench, it hasn’t solved the Riemann hypothesis, and it can’t yet set up a million dollar business on its own, so it’s not a breakthrough and is just more of the same. In reality, once you’ve spent enough time working with it on real-world tasks, you realize just how special and groundbreaking this model truly is.

comments.author: @0xFDFA
comments.text:
The claim that "GPT-5 is now available to all ChatGPT users, including free-tier," is misleading and factually incorrect. As confirmed during a detailed conversation with ChatGPT itself, free users currently do not have access to GPT-5—only Plus and Pro subscribers do. Despite the public messaging, free-tier users are stuck with GPT-4o, and no amount of complex questions will route them to GPT-5.

What’s more frustrating is that even ChatGPT initially repeated the misleading line and only admitted the truth after persistent questioning. This kind of unclear or false communication seriously damages trust, especially for a black-box AI service where transparency is key. It makes you wonder what other claims might be exaggerated or inaccurate.
